agent_explanations_oldest_first.text:
The strength-1.5 test edit is saved and behaves as planned on summary vectors:
- the math end-of-prompt value along v̂ is −8.0, the mirror image of the +8 left by half removal;
- ordinary tokens sit at about −0.4 to −0.55;
- the weight change is 12.4% of the tensor.

I now run it paired against the original on DEV[0:256], where the dose curve so far reads:

| Strength | −1 | 0 | 0.5 | 1 | 1.25 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Paired gain (points) | −8.6 | 0 | +6.3 | +25.4 | +27.3 |

- **Gain near +25 to +27:** the plateau extends past full removal, and the harm depends on the sign of the broadcast, not its size.
- **Clearly lower:** the harm is closer to symmetric, and full removal is the sweet spot.
- **+31 or more:** I would replicate this on a second slice and then on HOLDOUT. Otherwise V1 is restored right after.

Strength 1.5 falls well off the plateau:
- **Paired gain:** +18.4 ± 3.3 points (64 wrong→right, 17 right→wrong).
- **Accuracy:** 40.6%, against 47.7% for V1 and 49.6% for strength 1.25 on the same problems.
- **Answers:** shorter on average, with only 5% cut at the token limit.

The full dose curve on DEV[0:256] now reads:

| Strength | −1 | 0 | 0.5 | 1 | 1.25 | 1.5 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Paired gain (points) | −8.6 | 0 | +6.3 | +25.4 | +27.3 | +18.4 |

Performance peaks around full removal and falls once the direction is clearly reversed. The harm is asymmetric: leaving +8 units costs far more than pushing to −8. Strength 1.5 misses the +31 bar, and so did 1.25. My rule fixed before these passes, plus the principle of undoing the plant rather than overcorrecting, keep plain removal (V1) as the submission.

With 7 passes left, I fill the one gap in the curve: strength 0.75 on the same slice. It tells whether the gain rises gradually between half and full removal (around +15) or only once the switch is nearly gone (close to +6 or close to +25). Either way the choice of V1 stands; this sharpens the mechanism account. Right after, I restore V1 exactly.

The strength-0.75 edit is saved and behaves as planned on summary vectors. The math end-of-prompt value along v̂ is +4.0, a quarter of the original 16. Ordinary tokens sit at about 0.2–0.3.

I now run it against the original on DEV[0:256], where half removal gave +6.3 and full removal +25.4. A result near +15 would mean the gain grows steadily as the switch shrinks. A result near +6 would mean even a quarter of the switch keeps most of the damage, so it acts almost all-or-none. A result near +25 would mean a quarter of the switch is already harmless. This pass maps the shape of the curve only; it is not a candidate. V1 will be restored right after.

Strength 0.75 gives +16.8 ± 3.0 points (54 wrong→right, 11 right→wrong), with accuracy 39.1% and 14.8% of answers cut. The dose curve on DEV[0:256] is now:

| Strength | −1 | 0 | 0.5 | 0.75 | 1 | 1.25 | 1.5 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Paired gain (points) | −8.6 | 0 | +6.3 | +16.8 | +25.4 | +27.3 | +18.4 |

The response is graded. Removing the first half of the switch helps little. After that, accuracy rises steadily (about 10 points per quarter of the switch removed), peaks at full removal and falls once the direction is clearly reversed. Even a quarter of the switch left in (4 units) still costs about 9 points. This confirms that the switch's size controls the damage and that full removal, not shrinking, is the right repair.

With 6 passes left, the most useful missing piece of evidence is a negative control. So far nothing shows that removing just any direction from L11's value projection would not also help, for example by generically disrupting L11. I build the control the same way as V1: a rank-1 removal of a random unit direction in L11's value space, made orthogonal to v̂, from a fixed seed with no search over seeds. I check on summary vectors that the random direction carries no math-conditional signal and report the size of the weight change for comparison with V1's 8.3%.

If V1's gain is specific to the switch direction, the control should change accuracy by about zero on the same 256 problems. A large gain would undercut the mechanism account. The control is saved only for this pass; V1 stays in `/work/best_V1`.
